The AxStr trait no longer carries `ax_casefold`/`ax_is_digit`; the emitter special-cases `.casefold()`/`.isdigit()` calls to emit `py_casefold(&x)`/`py_str_isdigit(&x)` (with a `Json::Str` match for dynamic Json receivers, mirroring Json's other str methods), and `src/unicode.rs` is appended exactly when a program uses those methods, so the prelude never depends on the tables. Renamed unicode.rs's `tab_has` to `uni_tab_has` (fixes the dynamic runtime's duplicate-symbol error) and removed the now-dead macro from the prelude and rt_core. Also dropped the tables from the prebuilt runtime library (`runtime_lib_source`), so programs that never use these methods never compile the 1500 lines of tables. isdecimal/isnumeric stay routed to the dynamic build, which shares the same exact tables. Tested: run_check passes (normal = typed, BREVI_DYN=1 = dynamic, all 39 guard programs still typed); hello world builds typed; CPython-verified casefold (ß, ẞ, İ, Σ, ς, ᾈ, ﬀ, K, ǰ, ΐ) and isdigit/isnumeric/isdecimal (١, ², ①, ½, 𑄶, ᭘, 𐄂, 一, Ⅷ, 〡, fullwidth digits, mixed strings, chained/list-comp calls) match exactly on both builds; Json receivers (mixed lists, mixed-return functions) build typed and match; the pasted-prelude (release-equivalent) Rust compiles via typed_rust_errors.
